rows.quote: For breast cancer, we used GWAS summary statistics combining studies from the BCAC as well as other GWAS studies, containing 10.8 million SNPs from 133,384 cases and 113,789 controls of European ancestry [24].
rows.reference_quote: Zhang H Ahearn TU Lecarpentier J Barnes D Beesley J Qi G Genome-wide association study identifies 32 novel breast cancer susceptibility loci from overall and subtype-specific analyses Nat Genet 2020 52 6 572 581 10.1038/s41588-020-0609-2 32424353 PMC7808397
rows.coder_note: Rule E: ref 24 is Zhang 2020 (DOI verified; three dictionary rows) and the sentence gives 133,384 cases and 113,789 controls, BCAC plus other GWAS, the counts of the 'BCAC breast cancer subtypes (Zhang 2020)' row only; the row is outside the listed candidates. The Michailidou 2017 counts in the same passage describe the separate ER-subtype data the paper calls OncoArray + iCOGS + GWAS, not the BCAC data, so no conflict (rule H).

rows.quote: For the clustering analysis, we meta-analysed BMI GWAS summary statistics meta-analysis results from FinnGen (release 9) [21] and the GIANT consortium (2018 release) [22].
rows.coder_note: 'FinnGen (release 9)' is R9 (rule A); the 266,130 individuals given next is a trait-specific N that equals no other release's N (rule H).

The sentence says 'the GIANT consortium (2018 release) [22]': ref 22 is Locke 2015 (doi 10.1038/nature14177) and the next sentence's 322,154 Europeans is the exact N of 'GIANT BMI European (Locke 2015)', but the stated release year 2018 is that of the Yengo 2018 row and not of Locke 2015; release year against citation and N.

rows.quote: Breast cancer cases in the UK biobank were defined using data from cancer registries on cancer type, provided in ICD-9 or ICD-10 coding (data fields 40013 and 40006, respectively), as well as hospital in-patient data (data field 41202, 41203, 41204 and 41205) and cause of death (data fields 40001 and 40002).
rows.coder_note: Rule C: the authors' own analysis of UK Biobank individual-level data (one-sample MR by logistic regression on PGS), defined by the breast cancer phenotype (data fields) and the analytic sample of 361,887 Europeans; no published UK Biobank GWAS release is used and no dictionary row is such an analysis.
